summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of endometriosis, bipolar disorder, and chronic pelvic pain was admitted for acute on chronic left lower quadrant abdominal pain, similar to prior flares. Initial evaluation revealed hypokalemia, tachycardia, and mild anemia, with no signs of infection or acute abdominal pathology on ultrasound. Pain was managed with IV and oral medications, and fluids corrected electrolyte imbalances. A new subclinical hypothyroidism was noted, likely related to lithium, and a vaginal yeast infection was treated. The pain team adjusted her gabapentin and added ibuprofen. She improved clinically, with stable vitals and labs, and was discharged home with follow-up plans including colonoscopy, gynecology, pain management, and psychiatry visits.
